title: Fitness & Teamwork
subtitle: Five parts of fitness, and the reason a good team beats five good players.
objectives: Name the five components of health-related fitness
Tell health-related and skill-related fitness apart
Explain progressive overload and why rest is part of training
Explain what a role is in a team and why it matters

cards.eyebrow: Part 1 · What fitness is made of
cards.title: 'Fit' is not one thing
cards.text: A marathon runner and a powerlifter are both extremely fit, and neither could do the other's job.

cards.title: Health-related fitness, and how each is tested
cards.text: Tap through. The last button shows the skill-related group, which is different.

cards.title: Health-related fitness
cards.text: These five keep you well. Everyone needs them, whether or not they play a sport.

question.text: Doing as many push-ups as you can tests which component?
question.explain: Strength is one maximum effort. Endurance is repeating a sub-maximal one many times.

cards.title: Skill-related fitness
cards.text: Speed, power, agility, balance, coordination and reaction time. These help you play well rather than keep you healthy.
points: **You can be healthy** without any of them.

cards.title: A boxer trains from both lists
cards.text: Rounds need cardiovascular endurance. The punch needs power. Slipping a shot needs reaction time and agility.
points: **Pad work and sparring** build the skill side.
**That is why training has different days.**

question.text: Agility is one of the five health-related components of fitness.
question.explain: It is skill-related. The health-related five are endurance, strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition.

cards.title: Good place to pause
cards.text: Part 2 is how training is planned, and how teams work. Stand up for a moment.

cards.title: FITT: four dials on the same machine
cards.text: Frequency, Intensity, Time and Type. Every training plan you will ever see is these four settings.

cards.title: What each letter is
cards.text: Change one dial at a time. Changing all four at once is how people get injured.

cards.title: You adapt to what you survive
cards.text: Training works by asking slightly more than the body can currently do. The improvement happens afterwards, during rest.
points: **Progressive overload:** a little more, over time.
**The gain is built during recovery**, not during work.
**Rest days are part of the plan.**

cards.title: Sore is not the same as progress
cards.text: Muscle soreness peaks a day or two after hard work. It tells you what you did, not how much you gained.
points: **Pain in a joint is a stop sign**, not a badge.

question.text: What does the second T in FITT stand for?
question.explain: Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type. Change one dial at a time.

cards.title: A role is a promise about space
cards.text: In a team sport, your role tells everyone else where you will be. That is what lets them plan without talking.
points: **A team of five stars** with no roles collides.
**Communication fills the rest of the gaps.**

cards.title: Everyone chasing the objective loses
cards.text: In any team game, five players doing the same job leave four jobs undone. Sport works exactly the same way.
points: **Roles are not a limit on you.**
**They are a promise to the others.**
**Sportsmanship is part of it**, not extra.
**Losing well is a skill** you can practise.

question.text: Why do defined roles make a team faster?
options: Teammates can predict each other without talking
It reduces the number of rules
question.explain: Predictability is the whole point. Communication then fills whatever the roles do not cover.

terms.def: How long the heart and lungs can keep you going.
The force you can produce in one maximum effort.
How many times you can repeat a sub-maximal effort.
Speed, power, agility, balance, coordination, reaction time.
Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type. The four dials of a training plan.
Asking slightly more over time, so the body adapts.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Five health-related components.** Learn them in order.
**Skill-related is a separate list of six.**
**You adapt during rest**, not during work.

quiz.text: Which is a health-related component of fitness?
quiz.explain: The other three are skill-related. Health-related fitness is the list of five.
quiz.objective: Name the five components of health-related fitness

quiz.text: A timed run mainly tests which component?
quiz.explain: It measures how long the heart and lungs can keep you going.
quiz.objective: Name the five components of health-related fitness

quiz.text: What is the difference between muscular strength and muscular endurance?
options: Strength is one maximum effort; endurance is repeating a lighter one
Strength is for the legs and endurance for the arms
quiz.explain: One heavy lift tests strength. Push-ups to failure test endurance.
quiz.objective: Name the five components of health-related fitness

quiz.text: Which of these is skill-related fitness?
quiz.explain: Power is strength applied fast. It helps you play rather than keeping you well.
quiz.objective: Tell health-related and skill-related fitness apart

quiz.text: You can be in good health without strong skill-related fitness.
quiz.explain: True. Skill-related fitness helps performance. The health-related five are what keep you well.
quiz.objective: Tell health-related and skill-related fitness apart

quiz.explain: Four dials on the same machine. Change one at a time.

quiz.text: Adding a fourth session a week changes which FITT dial?
quiz.explain: Frequency is how often. Intensity is how hard and Time is how long.

quiz.text: Switching from running to swimming changes which dial?
quiz.explain: Type is what the activity actually is.

options: Gradually asking slightly more than the body can currently do
Training as hard as possible every session
Lifting the heaviest weight on day one
quiz.explain: A little more, over time. The adaptation itself happens during recovery.
quiz.objective: Explain progressive overload and why rest is part of training

quiz.text: The body gets stronger during the training session itself.
quiz.explain: False. Training causes the stress; the adaptation is built afterwards, during rest.
quiz.objective: Explain progressive overload and why rest is part of training

quiz.text: What does muscle soreness tell you?
options: What you did, not how much you gained
Exactly how much stronger you got
That you should train harder tomorrow
quiz.explain: Soreness is not a score. Steadily added load is the score.
quiz.objective: Explain progressive overload and why rest is part of training

quiz.text: Why does a team need defined roles?
options: So teammates can predict each other without talking
So fewer people have to run
So the coach has less to do
quiz.explain: Roles create predictability, and predictability creates speed.
quiz.objective: Explain what a role is in a team and why it matters

teacher.summary: Week 9 covers the PE strand on fitness and teamwork. The two fitness lists are kept strictly apart, because the exam tends to test exactly that boundary — agility and reaction time are skill-related, not health-related. FITT is taught as four independent dials, with the practical warning to change one at a time. The overload card makes the point that adaptation happens during rest, which is the single most useful thing a training child can know, and the soreness card actively pushes back on 'sore means it worked'. The teamwork section defines a role as a promise about space rather than a restriction, which is the framing most likely to land with him.
discussion: Ask him to name which FITT dial his own training changed most recently.
Ask which of the five health-related components his sport neglects.
Ask why soreness is a bad measure of progress and what a better one would be.
Ask what happens in a game when two players take the same role.
teacher.extension: Have him write a one-week training plan for himself using FITT explicitly, with one rest day marked and a reason for it.
misconceptions: 'Agility is health-related fitness.' It is skill-related. The health list is the five.
'Rest days are wasted days.' Adaptation happens during rest; without it, training only accumulates damage.
'Sore muscles mean a good session.' Soreness reflects novelty and damage, not gains.
'A team of the best players is the best team.' Without roles, five strong players duplicate each other's work.
